Thermostat makers push firmware fix after weekend outage

Published 2026-10-06 16:30 UTC

Several smart thermostat makers spent the weekend scrambling after a faulty software update left thousands of devices stuck in eco mode. Owners woke on Saturday to cold houses, with thermostats ignoring schedules and refusing manual changes from both the wall unit and the companion app.

The problem traced back to a configuration file pushed to devices on Friday evening. The file was meant to adjust energy-saving defaults for the coming winter, but a formatting error caused the thermostats to treat eco mode as a locked setting. Because the devices check for new settings each night, the bad file spread quickly before anyone noticed.

The companies involved began pushing a firmware fix on Sunday afternoon. Most thermostats installed it automatically within a few hours, though some owners had to restart their devices by removing them from the wall plate. One manufacturer said about 4 percent of affected units still needed a manual reset on Monday.

Customers were frustrated that the thermostats had no obvious way to override the setting locally. Several owners said the only way to get heat was to switch their furnace to emergency mode at the breaker panel. Consumer groups said the episode shows why connected home devices need a simple local fallback that works without the manufacturer's servers.

The manufacturers apologized and said they would add automated checks to catch malformed configuration files before release. One company promised a staged rollout process so future changes reach a small group of devices first. Another said it would offer account credits to customers who contacted support during the weekend.

Energy analysts noted the irony that a feature intended to cut household heating bills ended up costing some people money, since emergency heat strips use far more electricity than a heat pump running normally. Regulators in two states said they were looking into whether the companies met their obligations under connected device consumer protection rules.
